questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these tests use test doubles, or in how they exercise the service? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The tests use a hand-written InMemoryReadingStore for ReadingStore but a Mockito mock for AlertPublisher. Which reasoning best fits that choice?
choices: Mockito cannot mock interfaces that return Optional
Fakes are always preferable to mocks, so the mock for alerts is an oversight
The store's behaviour (keep only the newest reading) decides outcomes and is asserted through its state, while publishing an alert is an outgoing call best verified as an interaction
A fake is needed whenever a class has more than one method

questions.prompt: Suppose the fake store were replaced by an unconfigured Mockito mock of ReadingStore in readingAboveThresholdPublishesAlertCarryingTheDeviceThreshold. What would happen?
choices: saveIfNewer returns false by default, so ingest returns STALE and no alert is published, failing the test
The test would pass unchanged because the service only reads from the store
Mockito would throw as soon as saveIfNewer is called without a stubbing
The alert would be published but the stored reading would be null

questions.prompt: Why does the alert test use an ArgumentCaptor rather than verify(alerts).publish(any(Alert.class))?
choices: any() would make the verification fail if publish is called more than once
The captor lets the test inspect the Alert that was actually passed, confirming its threshold comes from the device profile and not from the reading
The captor makes Mockito stub publish so that it returns a value
verify cannot be used on void methods without a captor
